title: packages export: a read-only base's own export carries its .custom pair's object extension merged into the object, where ADR-0146 D8 item 3 says the base exports unchanged
body:
domain:devx#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbXGDmSYVyFomEEAdU3

Filing gate: ① a measured contract break with a named landing point (reach: `GET /api/v1/packages/BASE/export` on a stock showcase boot, reproduced twice).
Business reason: an operator customizes a vendor package (adds `region__c` to `showcase_task` through Studio's Customize, which writes an extension into `com.example.showcase.custom`) and then exports the base. The base file now carries the customer's field and relabel as if the vendor shipped them, so it can no longer be redeployed as the vendor's package, and installing it beside the pair's own export (which carries the same extension as `objectExtensions`) adds the field twice from two packages. #29563 and #29649 fixed this class for dashboards, reports and other overridable types; objects with an extension are the face still open.
Reader who acts: `domain:server`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` (`assemblePackageManifest`, L3454, the `ownDocumentsOf` filter after #29563 / #29649).
Dedupe (open and closed): `base export extension customization pair` 30 hits, `export carries extension ADR-0146 D8` 4. Nearest: #29563 (closed: the base export carried a published dashboard or report override), #29649 (closed: an override removed the base's item from its export), #28574 (closed: extensions export as `objectExtensions`), #29872 (open: an install-local package's export omits its `objectExtensions`, the second hop). None covers a base export that carries the pair's extension.

QA-source: #29893 · studio-authoring.package-extension-field-c · observed beside the clauses

## What happens

Measured at framework `589049b0` (main, 2026-11-03) on a fresh stock showcase boot, as admin.

1. `GET /api/v1/packages/com.example.showcase/export` → baseline: `data.objects[name=showcase_task].fields` has no `region__c`; `assignee.label` is "Assignee".
2. `POST /api/v1/packages/com.example.showcase/ensure-customization` → 201.
3. `PUT /api/v1/meta/object_extension/showcase_task?mode=draft&package=com.example.showcase.custom` `{"extend":"showcase_task","fields":{"region__c":{"type":"text","label":"Region"}}}` → 200.
4. `POST /api/v1/packages/com.example.showcase.custom/publish-drafts` `{}` → published.
5. `GET /api/v1/packages/com.example.showcase/export` again.
6. **Expected:** the base's `showcase_task` unchanged from step 1 (ADR-0146 D8 item 3: "`GET /packages/hotcrm/export` carries the base unchanged"); the extension travels only in `GET /packages/com.example.showcase.custom/export` as `objectExtensions`.
7. **Actual:** the base's `showcase_task.fields` now has `region__c`. In the first run, which had also published `tier__c` and a base-field label patch (`assignee` → "Assignee QA7") in the same extension, the base export carried all three. The pair's export carries the same extension in `objectExtensions` as well.

## Likely mechanism (read at 589049b0)

For `objects`, the per-package layer `assemblePackageManifest` reads serves the registry's object for the owner's name, and the registry folds the pair's `extend` contributor into that object. `ownDocumentsOf` (#29563 / #29649) drops an item that declares it overrides the package, but an extension is merged into the base's object rather than listed as a separate item, so there is nothing for that filter to drop. The base's own document is its code artifact, as #29649 already reads for other types.
